"'''Party All the Time'''" is a song by comedian and actor [[Eddie Murphy]], written and produced by [[Rick James]]. It was the [[lead single]] from Murphy's 1985 debut musical album ''[[How Could It Be]]''.<ref name="MurphyBoombox">{{cite web|author=Preezy|url=https://theboombox.com/eddie-murphy-how-could-it-be-album/|title=Five Best Songs From Eddie Murphy's 'How Could It Be' Album|publisher=[[The Boombox]]|date=July 20, 2015|access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref> It reached number two on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for three weeks, behind "[[Say You, Say Me]]" by [[Lionel Richie]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/1985-12-28/hot-100 | title=Party All the Time | work=Billboard.com}}</ref> The song also reached the top 40 in several other countries, being a top-ten hit in Canada, New Zealand and West Germany.

"Party All the Time" is a song by comedian and actor Eddie Murphy, written and produced by Rick James. It was the lead single from Murphy's 1985 debut musical album How Could It Be. It reached number two on the Billboard Hot 100 for three weeks, behind "Say You, Say Me" by Lionel Richie. The song also reached the top 40 in several other countries, being a top-ten hit in Canada, New Zealand and West Germany.

sections.heading: Production
sections.wikitext:
When Murphy informed actor/comedian [[Richard Pryor]] that he was doing an album, Pryor offered him a $100,000 bet that Murphy wouldn't be able to do a purely musical album without jokes. In a 2023 appearance on ''[[Jimmy Kimmel Live!]]'', Murphy said that Pryor never paid him the money before his death in 2005.<ref>{{cite news|title=Eddie Murphy has not forgotten his $100k bet with Richard Pryor: 'He owes me'|url=https://ew.com/eddie-murphy-not-forgotten-100-bet-richard-pryor-8409215|newspaper=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=30 November 2023|access-date=18 May 2024|last1=Holub|first1=Christian}}</ref> 

The single was recorded at Rick James's home studio in [[Buffalo, New York]], during what would go on to be named Buffalo's "Six-Pack" storm (named after a quote from Mayor [[James D. Griffin]]), where 33 inches of snow and 50 mile per hour wind speeds shut down the city.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McKinley |first=Dave |title=40th anniversary of the 1985 Blizzard, Buffalo's 'Six-Pack' storm |url=https://www.wgrz.com/article/weather/40th-anniversary-blizzard-1985-buffalo-6-pack-storm/71-34e52ceb-b31d-4940-bd66-98274edac210#:~:text=A%20multi%2Dday%20blizzard%20with,from%20Buffalo's%20most%20quotable%20mayor.&text=BUFFALO%2C%20N.Y.,a%20bout%20of%20bad%20weather. |website=wgrz.com}}</ref> 

Originally only planning to stay in Buffalo for a weekend to record the song, Murphy ended up being stuck inside with James for two weeks.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=07hqWMcLWI8 |title=Eddie Murphy on Getting Snowed in at Rick James' House, Michael Jackson Impersonation & You People |date=2023-01-25 |last=Jimmy Kimmel Live |access-date=2025-01-19 |via=YouTube}}</ref> In addition to writing and producing the song, James also provided additional ad-libs and backing vocals.<ref name="MurphyBoombox"/>
sections.text:
When Murphy informed actor/comedian Richard Pryor that he was doing an album, Pryor offered him a $100,000 bet that Murphy wouldn't be able to do a purely musical album without jokes. In a 2023 appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, Murphy said that Pryor never paid him the money before his death in 2005. 

The single was recorded at Rick James's home studio in Buffalo, New York, during what would go on to be named Buffalo's "Six-Pack" storm (named after a quote from Mayor James D. Griffin), where 33 inches of snow and 50 mile per hour wind speeds shut down the city. 

Originally only planning to stay in Buffalo for a weekend to record the song, Murphy ended up being stuck inside with James for two weeks. In addition to writing and producing the song, James also provided additional ad-libs and backing vocals.

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext:
A reader in the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', Barbara Bryson, criticized the song, characterizing it as "[[Gumby]] goes disco" (referring to the character parodied by Murphy on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''). The publication also placed the song at number one on "The Video Bottom 10" list.<ref name="TLAT">{{cite news|last1=Bryson|first1=Barbara|title=The Video Bottom 10|work=The Los Angeles Times|date=February 6, 1986|quote=1-"Party All the Time," Eddie Murphy. "Ye Gods-Gumby goes disco"-Barbara Bryson, L.A.}}</ref> Meanwhile, critic Scott Benarde in the Ft. Lauderdale ''[[Sun-Sentinel]]'' awarded the song his worst single for 1985, calling it a "catchy uptempo dance number" but asserting that "Murphy adds nothing but his ego to it.  His voice is paper thin and buried in the mix.  Anyone could have sung that tune the way it was produced. Murphy should stick to imitating Gumby."<ref>{{cite news |first=Scott |last=Benarde |title=WRITER MAKES PICKS OF TERRIFIC, TERRIBLE IN POP/ROCK MUSIC  |work=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |page=3.D |date=December 29, 1985 |quote= |url= }}</ref>

The song's music video won best urban contemporary video award at the American Video Awards in November 1985.<ref>{{cite news |first= |last= |title=The Boss takes two to top video awards |work=[[Montreal Gazette]] |page=D4 |date=November 22, 1985 |quote= |url= }}</ref>

A reader in the Los Angeles Times, Barbara Bryson, criticized the song, characterizing it as "Gumby goes disco" (referring to the character parodied by Murphy on Saturday Night Live). The publication also placed the song at number one on "The Video Bottom 10" list. Meanwhile, critic Scott Benarde in the Ft. Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel awarded the song his worst single for 1985, calling it a "catchy uptempo dance number" but asserting that "Murphy adds nothing but his ego to it.  His voice is paper thin and buried in the mix.  Anyone could have sung that tune the way it was produced. Murphy should stick to imitating Gumby."

The song's music video won best urban contemporary video award at the American Video Awards in November 1985.

sections.heading: Certifications
Remixes and covers
sections.wikitext:
In 2006, [[House Music|house]] DJ and producer [[Sharam Tayebi]] of [[Deep Dish (band)|Deep Dish]] released a [[remix]] of the song, known simply as "PATT" (an acronym for "Party All the Time"),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=d3H0d_0pqOI |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211222/d3H0d_0pqOI |archive-date=2021-12-22 |url-status=live|title=Sharam - PATT|publisher=[[Ministry of Sound Australia|TMRW Music]]|date=November 29, 2006|access-date=June 14, 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref> which peaked at No. 8 on the [[UK Singles Chart]] on December 30, 2006<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/2061/sharam/|title=Sharam - PATT (Party All the Time)|publisher=[[UK Singles Chart]]|access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref> and at No. 4 on the [[Polish Music Charts|Polish Airplay Chart]] in early 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nielsenmusiccontrol.com/index_pol |title=Nielsen Music Control Airplay - Poland Top 5 |publisher=Nielsen Music Control on behalf of [[ZPAV]]|accessdate=17 February 2023 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070306120525/http://www.nielsenmusiccontrol.com/index_pol |archivedate=6 March 2007}}</ref> The song also peaked at number 87 on the Australian [[ARIA Charts]].<ref name="ARIA">{{cite Ryan|page=250}}</ref>

In 2014, [[Gwyneth Paltrow]] covered the song in the [[Glee (TV series)|''Glee'']] season 5 episode "[[New Directions (Glee)|New Directions]]".

In 2019, American progressive rock/metal band [[Thank You Scientist]] released a cover of the song, accompanied by a humorous music video.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hurley |first=Miles |title=Watch Thank You Scientist's Hilarious New Video for Their Eddie Murphy/Rick James Cover – The Poke Around |url=https://thepokearound.com/2019/11/15/thank-you-scientist-party-all-the-time-video/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191201041618/http://thepokearound.com/2019/11/15/thank-you-scientist-party-all-the-time-video/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=December 1, 2019 |access-date=2023-08-27 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2023, American boy band [[Big Time Rush (group)|Big Time Rush]] released their version of the song titled "I Just Want To (Party All the Time)" for their album ''[[Another Life (Big Time Rush album)|Another Life]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aversa |first=Ralphie |date=June 5, 2023 |title=Big Time Rush returns with 'Another Life' and an unlikely assist from Rick James |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/music/2023/06/05/big-time-rush-new-album-another-life/70290665007/ |access-date=2023-06-12 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref>  Also in 2023 a remix by [[Hannah Laing]] and HVRR reached number 51 in the [[UK Singles Chart]].<ref name="off">{{cite web |title=HANNAH LAING Songs |url=https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/64913/hannah-laing/ |website=[[Official Charts]] |access-date=21 January 2024 |archive-date=21 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240121225323/https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/64913/hannah-laing/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2026, American artist Sturgill Simpson (under his stage name Johnny Blue Skies) released a cover of the song as the ninth track on his album, Mutiny After Midnight, which explored disco themes alongside country styles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Broerman |first=Michael |date=2026-06-09 |title=Johnny Blue Skies Puts Extended 'Mutiny After Midnight' On Streaming For His Birthday |url=https://liveforlivemusic.com/news/johnny-blue-skies-mutiny-after-midnight-streaming/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=L4LM |language=en-US}}</ref>
sections.text:
In 2006, house DJ and producer Sharam Tayebi of Deep Dish released a remix of the song, known simply as "PATT" (an acronym for "Party All the Time"), which peaked at No. 8 on the UK Singles Chart on December 30, 2006 and at No. 4 on the Polish Airplay Chart in early 2007. The song also peaked at number 87 on the Australian ARIA Charts.

In 2014, Gwyneth Paltrow covered the song in the Glee season 5 episode "New Directions".

In 2019, American progressive rock/metal band Thank You Scientist released a cover of the song, accompanied by a humorous music video.

In 2023, American boy band Big Time Rush released their version of the song titled "I Just Want To (Party All the Time)" for their album Another Life.  Also in 2023 a remix by Hannah Laing and HVRR reached number 51 in the UK Singles Chart.

In 2026, American artist Sturgill Simpson (under his stage name Johnny Blue Skies) released a cover of the song as the ninth track on his album, Mutiny After Midnight, which explored disco themes alongside country styles.
